sections.overview: Homo sapiens evolved in Africa about 300,000 years ago. It is the only human species alive today.
sections.identification: Compared with earlier humans, its skeleton is generally lighter, and its skull has a high rounded vault, a near-vertical forehead, reduced brow ridges and smaller jaws and teeth.
sections.habitat: The species originated in Africa and now occurs worldwide, occupying an exceptionally broad range of terrestrial and coastal environments.
sections.diet: Humans are dietary generalists: populations have gathered, hunted, fished and eaten diverse plant and animal foods, and many later adopted food production.
sections.behavior: Its history includes toolmaking, complex social networks and symbolic activities.
sections.reproduction: Children remain dependent on adult care for an unusually prolonged period after weaning.
sections.ecology: Homo sapiens is closely related to extinct human species such as Neanderthals, with which it interbred; genomic evidence also shows the persistence of Neanderthal ancestry in many living populations.
sections.conservation: Human activity has transformed environments and created new survival challenges for other species.
